paragraphs.en: The information crisis
paragraphs.zh: 信息危机

paragraphs.en: I believe these interlinked crises are driven and compounded by the digital revolution.
paragraphs.zh: 我认为，这场环环相扣的多重危机，由数字革命催生并不断加剧。

paragraphs.en: We are in the midst of an historic transition from one era to another.
paragraphs.zh: 我们正处在一场跨越时代的历史性转型之中。

paragraphs.en: In her recent book, Don't Burn Anyone at the Stake Today, Naomi Alderman makes a convincing case that what we face today is an information crisis, with very few precedents in human history.
paragraphs.zh: 娜奥米·奥尔德曼在新作《今日切勿将任何人火刑处死》中有力论证，我们当下遭遇的是一场人类史上罕见的信息危机。

paragraphs.en: "We live in a tidal wave of data," she writes. But we lack the "social and informational structures to manage it".
paragraphs.zh: “我们淹没在海量数据的浪潮之中，”她写道。但我们缺少“能够管控数据的社会与信息体系”。

paragraphs.en: This tidal wave of data contains much that is valuable, but that doesn't prevent it from being destabilising.
paragraphs.zh: 这股数据洪流中固然存在大量有价值的内容，却依旧会造成社会动荡。

paragraphs.en: Digital technology means that we are constantly being made aware of all the things we don't know, writes Alderman.
paragraphs.zh: 奥尔德曼写道，数字技术让我们无时无刻不意识到自身知识的局限。

paragraphs.en: "We might end up expressing an idea online that we've heard many times in our social circle, only to be jumped on by 50 people who know more and tell us that our ideas are stupid, old-fashioned and even prejudiced."
paragraphs.zh: “我们或许只是在网上说出一条圈子里反复听闻的观点，转眼就会遭到五十个知之更多的人围攻，他们指责我们的想法愚蠢、落伍，甚至带有偏见。”

paragraphs.en: It also works the other way round.
paragraphs.zh: 反之亦然。

paragraphs.en: "When we can see everyone else's opinions, it turns out that someone we really liked may hold an idea that we find stupid, old-fashioned or even prejudiced.
paragraphs.zh: “当我们能看见所有人的观点时，会发现某个我们曾经十分喜爱的人，怀揣着我们眼中愚蠢、落伍、甚至带有偏见的想法。

paragraphs.en: It's the 'I used to like Uncle Bob until I saw his posts on Facebook' syndrome. We're left wondering who we can trust."
paragraphs.zh: 这就是那种‘我曾经很喜欢鲍勃叔叔，直到我看见他脸书的动态’式困境。我们不禁疑惑，究竟还能相信谁。”

paragraphs.en: This feeling of being forever assailed by new and disorienting information leads people to feel defensive, alone and angry.
paragraphs.zh: 持续不断涌入的陌生、令人迷茫的信息，让人们心生戒备、倍感孤独、怒火丛生。

paragraphs.en: Now if all we had to worry about was a deluge of accurate new information at our fingertips, perhaps we would not be facing a crisis of such magnitude.
paragraphs.zh: 倘若我们只需应对随手可得的海量真实信息，或许这场危机不会演变到如此严重的地步。

paragraphs.en: But as we know, the world is full of bad actors actively stoking the information crisis.
paragraphs.zh: 但我们心知肚明，世上充斥着别有用心之人，刻意煽动这场信息危机。

paragraphs.en: No one is more aware of this than journalists.
paragraphs.zh: 记者群体对此体会最为深刻。

paragraphs.en: One measure of the importance of this work is how far the powerful will go to shut it down: through censorship, or legal persecution, or by polluting the information environment with the help of trolls, bots and propagandists, so that the truth becomes impossible to discern.
paragraphs.zh: 新闻工作的重要性，从掌权者不择手段打压媒体的行径便可见一斑：实施审查、发起司法迫害，或是借助网络水军、机器人账号、宣传人员污染信息环境，令真相无从分辨。

paragraphs.en: ("Flood the zone with shit," as Steve Bannon infamously put it.)
paragraphs.zh: （史蒂夫·班农那句臭名昭著的言论恰如其分：“用垃圾信息淹没舆论场。”）

paragraphs.en: At its most extreme, opponents of the truth simply kill their enemies.
paragraphs.zh: 极端情况下，真相的反对者会直接杀害异见人士。

paragraphs.en: Last year, 129 journalists and media workers were killed.
paragraphs.zh: 去年，共有129名记者与媒体从业人员遇害。

paragraphs.en: That is the highest figure since the Committee to Protect Journalists began collecting data more than 30 years ago.
paragraphs.zh: 这是保护记者委员会三十余年统计数据里的最高纪录。

paragraphs.en: Fifty-four of those killed were Palestinian journalists in Gaza; nine were killed in Sudan, and four in Ukraine.
paragraphs.zh: 遇难者中有54名是加沙的巴勒斯坦记者；9人死于苏丹，4人死于乌克兰。

paragraphs.en: There was once a broadly upheld convention that a press vest gave some level of protection in a war zone.
paragraphs.zh: 曾经有一条普遍公认的准则：战地记者的媒体标识能为其提供一定保护。

paragraphs.en: No longer.
paragraphs.zh: 如今这条准则已然失效。

paragraphs.en: These efforts to prevent journalists from doing their work are not new, even if they are becoming more common.
paragraphs.zh: 打压记者正常工作的手段由来已久，只是如今愈发频繁。

paragraphs.en: The thing that has truly brought us into this age of information crisis is technology.
paragraphs.zh: 而真正将我们推入这场信息危机时代的，是科技本身。

paragraphs.en: It is hardly controversial, these days, to note that so much digital technology seems designed to produce conflict, to prioritise lies over truth.
paragraphs.zh: 如今几乎无人否认，大量数字技术的设计初衷仿佛就是制造对立，优先推送谎言而非真相。

paragraphs.en: Rather than unlocking the best in human nature, it seems designed to stoke the worst in us.
paragraphs.zh: 这类技术并未释放人性中的美好，反倒不断煽动人性之恶。

paragraphs.en: As the tech critic Jacob Silverman says: "Today's internet isn't really designed for us, but rather to elicit certain responses from us [that] are hostile to human flourishing."
paragraphs.zh: 科技评论家雅各布·西尔弗曼说道：“当下的互联网并非为人类本身设计，而是为了诱导人类产生不利于自我良性发展的负面情绪与行为。”

paragraphs.en: It is not incidental that the big tech companies are run by a very narrow sliver of humanity: wealthy men, overwhelmingly based on the west coast of the US.
paragraphs.zh: 大型科技企业的掌权者群体高度单一绝非偶然：大多是定居美国西海岸的富裕男性。

paragraphs.en: These companies crave enormous profits, and have little regard for the public good.
paragraphs.zh: 这些企业追逐巨额利润，几乎无视公共利益。

paragraphs.en: Most are happy to suck up to demagogues if it's good for business.
paragraphs.zh: 只要利于营收，多数企业甘愿迎合煽动民粹的政客。

paragraphs.en: Elon Musk even briefly joined the Trump administration, slashing public spending and gutting USAID.
paragraphs.zh: 埃隆·马斯克甚至曾短暂加入特朗普政府，大幅削减公共开支、裁撤美国国际开发署。

paragraphs.en: Today, Musk spends much of his time posting nativist conspiracy theories to his almost 240 million followers on the social media platform that he owns and that has been engineered to promote conflict and extremism (one of the many reasons the Guardian as an institution came off X in 2024).
paragraphs.zh: 如今，马斯克大半时间都在自家社交媒体平台上，向近2.4亿粉丝发布本土主义阴谋论，而该平台的算法设计本就助长冲突与极端思想（这也是《卫报》在2024年集体退出X平台的诸多原因之一）。
